question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $v(x)={5}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {5}^{x}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot ({5}^{x})^{′}}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot {5}^{x}-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot {5}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡5)}{{({5}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{{5}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$
